items.headline: Government Appeals CIT Refund Order, Challenges Commissioner Testimony
items.summary: The Trump administration filed an appeal on June 2, 2026, challenging the Court of International Trade's universal IEEPA refund order requiring CBP to refund $166 billion in tariffs. The government also filed for expedited ruling on CBP Commissioner testimony before the June 9 hearing, potentially creating uncertainty for ongoing refund processes.

items.headline: CBP Reports $85B in CAPE Refund Claims Accepted, $20.6B Processed
items.summary: As of May 26, CBP received 157,402 CAPE declarations with 70% passing validation. Approximately 15.9 million entries passed validation and $85 billion in refunds accepted for processing. CBP has already processed $20.6 billion through the CAPE refund system, showing significant progress in Phase 1 implementation.

items.headline: CAPE Phase 1 ACH Payments Begin Hitting Bank Accounts
items.summary: CBP confirmed in CSMS #68536553 that ACH refund payments could begin as early as May 12, 2026, with media reports suggesting some importers are already receiving refunds. However, millions of entries face delays due to ACH enrollment issues, data mismatches, and validation errors requiring immediate attention from importers.

items.headline: CIT Strikes Down Section 122 Replacement Tariffs as Unlawful
items.summary: The Court of International Trade ruled Section 122 tariffs invalid in Oregon v. United States, determining the administration's balance-of-payments justification was insufficient. This creates potential for additional refund claims as the 10% (now 15%) replacement tariffs face their own legal challenges alongside the IEEPA refund process.

items.headline: CBP Officially Launches CAPE Portal for IEEPA Refund Claims
items.summary: CBP activated Phase 1 of the CAPE system in ACE Portal, allowing importers and brokers to file refund declarations. Phase 1 covers unliquidated entries and entries within 80 days of liquidation. The system processes refunds on a consolidated basis rather than entry-by-entry, with expected processing times of 60-90 days absent compliance concerns.

items.headline: Government Appeal Deadline Approaches for Universal Refund Order
items.summary: The government's deadline to appeal the CIT's nationwide refund order extends through approximately June 6, 2026. A successful appeal could result in a stay of the refund process and significantly delay payments for all importers, making this a critical watch date for the trade community and financial markets.

items.headline: Consumer Class Actions Proliferate Against Major Brands and Retailers
items.summary: Two dozen class action lawsuits have been filed against companies like Costco, FedEx, and Lululemon, alleging unjust enrichment from IEEPA tariff pass-through to consumers. Plaintiffs seek to capture shares of refunds, creating new litigation risk for importers who increased prices based on the now-invalidated tariffs.

items.headline: Section 122 Replacement Tariffs Set to Expire July 24, 2026
items.summary: The 15% Section 122 tariffs (increased from initial 10%) that replaced IEEPA have a hard expiration date of July 24, 2026. With no Congressional action to extend and ongoing legal challenges, importers face uncertainty about post-July tariff landscape. The administration prefers permanent statutory replacement through Section 301 investigations.
